mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant correlation with 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL index above 275 (indicating year-over-year inflation above 3.0%) triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 return, as it signals the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 275 does not lead to negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100.5 (indicating growth above the 2017 base) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a robust economy without excessive labor market tightness, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings growth is supported.
failure_condition: The condition (INDPRO > 100.5 and UNRATE < 4.0) occurs, but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 275), a federal funds rate above 0.5% signals that the Fed has not sufficiently eased, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as the economy faces a risk of recession due to restrictive policy.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 275), FEDFUNDS > 0.5% does not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as lower housing starts indicate weakening economic demand, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: HOUST level shows no significant correlation with 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which increases the risk of Fed tightening and wage inflation, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5 does not lead to negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1600 (thousands) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 600000 (millions), it signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are supported by strong consumption.
failure_condition: The condition (HOUST > 1600 and RSAFS > 600000) occurs, but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%) is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 returns, as it supports economic growth and reduces the cost of capital, leading to sustained equity outperformance.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% does not lead to positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
